extracted.intended_audience: researchers and systematic reviewers in health technology assessment and clinical research (interested in publication/citation/language bias and reasons for non-publication)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and classifying empirical evidence about language bias, citation bias, and reasons studies fail to be published (used in systematic reviews and health technology assessments). Includes categories used to code non-publication and metrics reported by empirical studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language bias – included empirical studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Heading listing empirical studies included that examine language bias (i.e., selective inclusion/publication of studies by language).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix lists multiple empirical studies that investigated whether language of publication influences inclusion in reviews or likelihood of publication; study-level measures reported include proportions, odds/relative measures, p-values and 95% CIs. Examples of reported metrics: proportions published in English vs non-English, p-values for comparisons, and confidence intervals for effect estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation bias – included empirical studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Heading listing empirical studies included that examine citation bias (i.e., selective citation of studies depending on their results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix lists multiple empirical investigations of citation bias; reported outcomes include proportion of studies cited, citation counts, and comparisons (percentages and CIs) of citation rates for positive vs negative findings. Examples include reported percentages of studies cited and statistics comparing citation frequency across study outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for non-publication (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall categorisation of reasons why studies were not prepared/submitted/published derived from multiple empirical surveys and cohorts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix collates reasons across many studies and presents frequencies/percentages (e.g., publication not an aim 48%, class project only 30%, assistant lost interest 26% in Cooper 1997) and similar breakdowns in other cohorts. Use as a coding frame for classifying non-publication in methodological research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication not an aim
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given for non-publication: the study was not intended to be prepared for journal publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported explicitly (e.g., Cooper 1997: 'Publication not an aim: 48%'). Use as a primary category when investigators state publication was not an objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class project only
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given for non-publication: the work was performed only as a class/project and not intended for journal submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in surveys (e.g., Cooper 1997: 'Class project only: 30%').

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant lost interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given for non-publication: the assistant or person responsible lost interest in preparing the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported frequency in multiple cohorts (e.g., Cooper 1997: 26%).

rubrics_metrics.name: No significant results / Negative results
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given for non-publication: results were not significant or negative and therefore not submitted/published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears across studies (e.g., Cooper: 'No significant results'; Decullier/Dickersin: 'Negative results'); used as evidence of outcome-related non-publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results were not interesting / Unimportant results
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: investigators judged the results not interesting or not important enough to publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported across cohorts (e.g., Cooper: 'Results were not interesting: 20%'; Easterbrook lists 'Unimportant results'). Use to code perceived lack of novelty or interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design or operational problems / Methodological limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: the study had design, logistical or methodological problems preventing publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in multiple studies (e.g., Cooper: 'Design or operational problems: 12%'; other cohorts list 'Methodological limitations'). Use when authors identify study quality or operational issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researchers did not recall / Does not recall / No reason given / Not provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: investigators could not recall or provided no reason for non-publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when respondents report no specific reason or fail to state one; reported in several surveys (percentages vary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Others lost interest / Co-author issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: other team members lost interest or co-author responsibility problems impeded manuscript preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes 'Others lost interest' (Cooper) and 'Too much trouble with co-authors', 'Co-author responsibility or lack of participation'. Reported frequencies in several cohorts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing or submission in progress / Manuscript in preparation / Manuscript under review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: manuscript was being written or submitted at time of survey (i.e., in progress).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears in several studies (e.g., Decullier/Dickersin 'Writing or submission in progress'; Krzyzanowska: 'Manuscript in preparation', 'under review'). Use to indicate delay rather than permanent non-publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Published in other forms / Different version published / Published elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: results were published in another format (e.g., other journal, report) or a different version was published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a reason for apparent non-publication in journal form; coding should distinguish alternative dissemination from non-publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper rejected / Rejection from peer-reviewed journal / Article not accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: manuscript was submitted but rejected by journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported across cohorts (percentages provided in tables). Use when rejection, not choice, prevents publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not available / Not provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: information about reason for non-publication was not available or the respondent did not provide it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat as missing data category when aggregating reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not interesting or no time / Lack of time / No time to prepare
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: investigators cited lack of time or low priority as the reason for not preparing/submitting a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequently reported (e.g., 'Lack of time', 'Too busy or lost interest', 'Low priority'); often the most common reason in many cohorts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-investigator/operational problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: problems with co-investigators or operational aspects of the study prevented completion/publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include collaborator withdrawal, disagreements, or operational difficulties cited in multiple cohort studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data analysis not completed / Analysis incomplete
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: data analysis was not completed and therefore manuscript not prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in several studies (e.g., 'Data analysis not completed', 'Analysis incomplete').

rubrics_metrics.name: Null results
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason category capturing null findings (no effect) as part of non-publication coding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Easterbrook and other studies separate 'null' from significant and non-significant; useful for coding outcome-based non-publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology or logistic problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: logistical or methodological problems in conducting the study prevented completion/publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears as an explicit reason in some cohorts; overlaps with 'design or operational problems' but retains original wording where used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor has control of data / Not in the sponsor’s interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: sponsor controls data or publication decisions; sponsor interest prevents publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when commercial or sponsor control limits dissemination ('Not in the sponsor’s interest' or 'Sponsor has control of data').

rubrics_metrics.name: Too busy or lost interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: primary investigator or team too busy or lost interest in pursuing publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported across multiple surveys; often categorized with low priority or lack of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-investigator left / Relocation of authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: key personnel left or relocated, impeding manuscript completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in several cohorts as personnel-change related barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of time/other resources / Insufficient priority / Lack of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: insufficient resources (time, funding, priority) to finish and publish the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate category capturing resource constraints referenced in many studies (e.g., 'Lack of time/other resources', 'Insufficient priority').

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript rejected by journal (summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate count/category: proportion of studies where the manuscript was submitted but rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in summary tables (e.g., 'Manuscript rejected by journal: 6 (5%)' in one cohort). Helpful when quantifying rejection vs non-submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results considered not interesting / Results considered not important enough
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: investigators believed the findings lacked sufficient interest or importance for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported explicitly in several cohort surveys; often overlaps with 'no significant results' but captures subjective appraisal of importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification of data after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: changes to data after abstract submission prevented subsequent journal publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in De Bellefeuille as a reason; use when post-submission changes hinder publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Too much trouble with co-authors / Difficulty with co-authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: conflicts or practical difficulties with co-authors impeded manuscript completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in Hashkes and other cohorts; distinct from mere co-author responsibility—relates to interpersonal/cooperation problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thought that journal was unlikely to accept / Fear of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: investigators believed journals unlikely to accept the manuscript and therefore did not submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in multiple studies as an anticipatory barrier to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Others published with similar findings / Other similar articles published
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: similar findings published by others reduced perceived need to publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited in Hashkes and others; indicates perceived redundancy as a reason to forgo submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study quality poor / Design perceived poor
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: perceived poor study quality discouraged pursuing publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when investigators self-report low study quality as the reason for non-publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results did not support the hypothesis / Analysis showed no support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reason given: findings did not support the original hypothesis, reducing motivation to publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a distinct reason in some surveys; overlaps with 'negative' or 'null' but preserves investigator rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors affecting publication of phase I clinical trials (list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific factors enumerated as affecting publication of phase I clinical trials: Lack of time; Manuscript in preparation; Relocation of authors; Incomplete study; Results considered not interesting; Rejection from peer-reviewed journal; Manuscript submitted; Not in the sponsor’s interest; Conflict of interest; Other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix presents counts for phase I trials (novel vs non-novel agents). Use as a targeted factor list for early-phase trial non-publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for failure to submit a manuscript to a journal (list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commonly listed reasons for not submitting manuscripts: No time to prepare for publication; Study still ongoing; Responsibility for manuscript belongs to a co-author; Difficulty with co-authors (lack of participation); Pursuit of publication given a low priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented in summary form (e.g., Sprague et al.); useful as a coding frame for non-submission specifically (as distinct from rejection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Different dissemination channels (published in other forms / reports / abstracts only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category capturing that findings were disseminated outside peer-reviewed journals (e.g., abstracts, reports, other formats) and thus not counted as journal publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to distinguish 'not published in peer-reviewed journal' from 'not disseminated at all'. Several studies report 'submitted or published elsewhere' frequencies.
